newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Top Hong Kong judge resigns for 1997 leadership run.
newsitem.headline: Top Hong Kong judge resigns for 1997 leadership run.

text.p: Hong Kong's top judge, Chief Justice Sir Ti Liang Yang, has resigned to run for the post of the territory's first chief executive after it reverts to China next year, the government said on Friday.

"In a letter to the governor, Sir Ti Liang stated that following his decision to accept nomination to the post Chief Executive of the Special Administrative Region of Hong Kong, constitutional propriety required him to resign from the post of Chief Justice," a government statement said.
Yang's resignation would take effect on November 4 upon expiration of his earned leave entitlement, it said.

Yang, 67, had been under pressure to resign as politicians and legal experts said his decision to run for chief executive created a conflict of interest and raised a question mark over his role in the British-style judiciary.
Hong Kong reverts to Chinese sovereignty at midnight June 30, 1997, after a century and a half as a British colony.
